example.ja: カフェでずっとおしゃべりしてた。
example.english: We sat chatting in a café the whole time.

examplePolite.romaji: Kafe de zutto oshaberi shite imashita.
examplePolite.ja: カフェでずっとおしゃべりしていました。
examplePolite.english: We sat chatting in a café the whole time.

notes: Said of a person it means a chatterbox or someone who can't keep a secret, often as a light tease.

use: Sounds a little formal; in casual talk people mostly just say hanasu (talk).

example.romaji: Kare to zenzen kaiwa ga tsuzukanai.
example.ja: 彼と全然会話が続かない。
example.english: I can never keep a conversation going with him.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare to wa zenzen kaiwa ga tsuzukimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 彼とは全然会話が続きません。
examplePolite.english: I can never keep a conversation going with him.

english: something to talk about; material, a joke
use: Casual word for a story, topic or joke you can use.

example.ja: 話すネタがなくなった。
example.english: I've run out of things to talk about.

examplePolite.romaji: Hanasu neta ga nakunarimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 話すネタがなくなりました。
examplePolite.english: I've run out of things to talk about.

notes: Netabare = spoiler; neta is also the fish on top of sushi.

use: Wadai no X = the much-talked-about X; wadai ni naru = become the talk of the town.

example.ja: ちょっと話題変えようか。
example.english: Let's change the subject.

examplePolite.romaji: Chotto wadai o kaemashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと話題を変えましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we change the subject?

use: Any reply, spoken or written, including answering when your name is called; often 'henji suru'.

example.romaji: Yonde mo henji shinai n da yo.
example.ja: 呼んでも返事しないんだよ。
example.english: He doesn't answer even when I call him.

examplePolite.romaji: Yonde mo henji o shinai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 呼んでも返事をしないんです。
examplePolite.english: He doesn't answer even when I call him.

notes: For texts and emails, henshin is more specific.

use: Usually 'henshin suru' or 'henshin ga kuru' (get a reply).

example.ja: 彼女からまだ返信来ない。
example.english: She still hasn't replied.

examplePolite.romaji: Kanojo kara mada henshin ga kimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女からまだ返信が来ません。
examplePolite.english: She still hasn't replied.

notes: Same sound as henshin 'transformation', as in superheroes.

use: How someone reacts to news, a joke or a message; hannou ga nai = no response.

example.ja: 彼の反応、どうだった？
example.english: How did he react?

examplePolite.romaji: Kare no hannou wa dou deshita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 彼の反応はどうでしたか？
examplePolite.english: How did he react?

example.romaji: Kore, minna ni wa himitsu ne.
example.ja: これ、みんなには秘密ね。
example.english: Keep this a secret from everyone, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: Kore wa minna ni wa himitsu ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: これはみんなには秘密にしてください。
examplePolite.english: Please keep this a secret from everyone.

notes: Himitsu ni suru = keep something secret.

use: Facts you find out or are told; often in thanks for a useful tip.

example.ja: 情報ありがとう、本当に助かった。
example.english: Thanks for the info, that really helped.

examplePolite.romaji: Jouhou arigatou gozaimasu, hontou ni tasukarimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 情報ありがとうございます、本当に助かりました。
examplePolite.english: Thanks for the information, it really helped.

use: Kiroku suru = write down, log; also a record in sport (shin kiroku = a new record).

example.ja: 毎日体重を記録してる。
example.english: I log my weight every day.

examplePolite.romaji: Mainichi taijuu o kiroku shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 毎日体重を記録しています。
examplePolite.english: I log my weight every day.

notes: For recording sound or video, say rokuon or rokuga.

example.ja: 昨日面白い記事読んだよ。
example.english: I read an interesting article yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou omoshiroi kiji o yomimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日面白い記事を読みました。
examplePolite.english: I read an interesting article yesterday.

notes: Same sound as kiji 'fabric' or 'dough' (生地); context makes it clear.

example.ja: これ、なんか間違いじゃない？
example.english: Isn't this some kind of mistake?

examplePolite.romaji: Kore wa nanika no machigai ja nai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: これは何かの間違いじゃないですか？
examplePolite.english: Isn't this some kind of mistake?

notes: Machigai nai = definitely, no doubt; the verb is machigaeru (get wrong).

english: the opposite; the other way round, reverse
use: Often 'gyaku ni' (actually, on the contrary) to flip what was just said.

example.romaji: Gyaku da yo, migi ja nakute hidari.
example.ja: 逆だよ、右じゃなくて左。
example.english: Other way round, it's left, not right.

examplePolite.romaji: Gyaku desu yo, migi ja nakute hidari desu.
examplePolite.ja: 逆ですよ、右じゃなくて左です。
examplePolite.english: It's the other way round: left, not right.

use: Two uses: being against something (hantai suru), and the opposite side or direction.

example.ja: 結婚、親に反対された。
example.english: My parents were against the marriage.

examplePolite.romaji: Kekkon o oya ni hantai saremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 結婚を親に反対されました。
examplePolite.english: My parents were against the marriage.

notes: Hantai gawa = the other side; for 'the reverse', gyaku is more natural.

use: Often said of a decision that turned out well: X shite seikai datta.

example.ja: 傘持ってきて正解だった。
example.english: Good thing I brought an umbrella.

examplePolite.romaji: Kasa o motte kite seikai deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 傘を持ってきて正解でした。
examplePolite.english: Good thing I brought an umbrella.

use: Sounds a bit formal; casually people ask dou omou? (what do you think?) instead.

example.ja: みんなの意見聞きたいな。
example.english: I'd like to hear what everyone thinks.

examplePolite.romaji: Minasan no iken o kikitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: みなさんの意見を聞きたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like to hear everyone's opinion.

use: Often 'X no tachiba ni naru' (put yourself in X's shoes).

example.romaji: Ore no tachiba mo kangaete yo.
example.ja: 俺の立場も考えてよ。
example.english: Think about my position too.

examplePolite.romaji: Watashi no tachiba mo kangaete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 私の立場も考えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please think about my position too.

notes: About your role and circumstances, not a physical position (ichi).

example.ja: 言い訳しないでよ。
example.english: Don't make excuses.

examplePolite.romaji: Iiwake wa shinai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 言い訳はしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't make excuses.

notes: Iiwake ja nai kedo... = I'm not making excuses, but...

use: Adobaisu suru = give advice; adobaisu o morau = get advice.

example.ja: なんかいいアドバイスある？
example.english: Got any good advice?

examplePolite.romaji: Nanika ii adobaisu wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何かいいアドバイスはありますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you have any good advice?

notes: More common in speech than the native word jogen.

english: pointless; no use; makes no sense
use: Casually shortened to imi nai, often as imi nai jan (that's pointless).

example.romaji: Imasara itte mo imi nai yo.
example.ja: 今さら言っても意味ないよ。
example.english: There's no point saying it now.

examplePolite.romaji: Imasara itte mo imi ga arimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: 今さら言っても意味がありませんよ。
examplePolite.english: There's no point saying it now.

notes: Imi wakannai = I don't get it, that makes no sense.
